Issue: Dish washer was filling and draining twice in a night. Samsung did some engineering and saved my house from flooding with water by turning on the drain pup automatically because of the old part failing to stop the inflow of water.

My way of install: There might be an easier way but... I disconnected power, water inlet, drain hose and removed the lose items inside of the washer. I then pulled the dishwasher out of the cabinet and put it on its back watching for any water leaking. Removed the front white cover plate behind the kick plate. Lifted straight forward on the circuit board back hosing. Then removed the two screws from each side of the plate behind where the electrical box was. Detached the white barbed connectors from the inside kick plate and rolled it forward and out. Unscrewed the inlet valve 90 degree brass fitting to reuse it on new part and then removed 3 screws holding valve in. Went to the mid left side and used needle nose pliers to move hose clamp and disconnected the 13mm ish black hose from the clear plastics part . Then was able to bring valve and hose forward enough to unhook electrical connector from inlet valve. Reused the black hose on new part. Reassembly was the reverse. I tightened the 90 degree brass fitting onto the new valve once the valve was screwed back into the washer so as to not fidget with the lose part. Of note the inner kick panel was a pain to get back in and reattached to the white barbed wire loom retainer. It took me about 30 to 45 minutes to get out fixed and back into the cabinet. Needle nose pliers, 2 screwdrivers, crescent wrench, pipe thread tape and 40 years of fixing stuff around the house.

Saved me from buying a new fridge. - Our 1994 Kenmore refrigerator quit cooling. I could hear it try to start but it would immediately shut back down. I recognized this as a symptom of a bad starter relay. Unfortunately the OEM part is obsolete. I ordered one of these starers and wired it in (very simple). The refrigerator started right up and has been running fine since.

If this happens to you and the OEM part is still available for your refrigerator it's better to use the original part (complicated engineering reason). But if you find yourself in my situation with no option other than buying a whole new refrigerator these work great. In fact, I'm buying another one just to have in case of an emergency so I don't lose food because of a refrigerator or freezer failure.

Keep in mind if you are thinking of buying one of these that they come with different capacities based on the size of the compressor you're trying to start. Also, more modern refrigerators or freezers use a run capacitor so they may require a model different from this one. Do your homework before ordering. On second thought if you don't know these things maybe you shouldn't be doing this.
